title: TAMIU petroleum engineering lands $3.8 million software donation
excerpt: Texas A&M International University's petroleum engineering program has received a software donation valued at $3,816,620 from Petroleum Experts, giving students access to industry-standard production modeling tools, according to TAMIU.
content:
Texas A&M International University's petroleum engineering program has received a software donation valued at $3,816,620 from Petroleum Experts, known as Petex, according to TAMIU.

The donation renews and continues educational licenses for Integrated Production Modeling software, an industry-standard suite used to model integrated oil and gas production systems, including reservoirs, wells and surface networks, according to TAMIU.

Associate professor of petroleum engineering Dr. Fatick Nath led the effort to secure the licenses, according to TAMIU. The university said the software will let students model comprehensive oil and gas production systems, strengthening hands-on learning, teaching, research and industry-focused training.

Petex, founded in 1990 and based in Scotland, develops engineering software for the petroleum industry and serves more than 400 clients worldwide, according to TAMIU. Its Houston office, Petroleum Experts Inc., facilitated the donation, and the company offers educational licenses to a limited number of universities with petroleum engineering programs.

TAMIU said students using the professional software will gain skills needed for employment in the petroleum engineering industry. The program sits within the university's School of Engineering, which also offers ABET-accredited undergraduate programs in systems engineering and computer engineering, along with a pre-engineering curriculum for transfer to other engineering programs.

More information about TAMIU's School of Engineering is available by calling 956.326.2669 or visiting tamiu.edu/coas/soen, according to TAMIU.

Sources:

  • TAMIU, "TAMIU Petroleum Engineering Program Receives $3.8M Software Donation," November 4, 2026
